text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between West Ham and Aston Villa at the London Stadium!
Ahead of today's game - the final Premier League fixture before next week's internationals - West Ham demolished Freiburg in the Europa League.

Keeping their dream of back-to-back continental titles alive, the London club ultimately cruised to a 5-1 aggregate success and booked a meeting with Bundesliga leaders Bayer Leverkusen in the quarter-finals.
Last time out in the English top flight, the Hammers fought back from two goals down to rescue a point against relegation-threatened Burnley, and they sit seventh in the standings.
Like their hosts, Aston Villa now return to domestic duty on the back of an emphatic European victory.
On Thursday, Unai Emery's men saw off Ajax in the Europa Conference League, and their 4-0 aggregate win set up a clash with Lille in next month's quarter-finals.
The Villans suffered a painful loss by the same scoreline in their most recent Premier League match, versus top-four rivals Tottenham Hotspur.
Following Spurs' subsequent defeat to Fulham, though, Villa can strengthen their grip on fourth place - victory today would increase their cushion to five points.

Despite the quick turnaround, David Moyes makes only two changes to the West Ham XI that crushed Freiburg: Areola returns in goal, while Emerson has been passed fit and replaces midweek goalscorer Cresswell at left-back.
Maxwel Cornet is the hosts' sole absentee, due to a thigh injury.
Though Aston Villa's top scorer Watkins lasted only 33 minutes against Ajax before succumbing to a knee injury, he is fit to start today, alongside Colombian striker Duran.
However, Villa captain John McGinn begins his three-match suspension today.
Konsa is back from a European ban and starts in defence, but Tyrone Mings, Emi Buendia, Boubacar Kamara and Jacob Ramsey all remain unavailable.
The players are out on the pitch, and kick-off in this claret-and-blue contest is now just moments away!
Aston Villa kick off, and we are under way at the London Stadium!

Following their 4-1 win at Villa Park in October, Aston Villa are looking to complete a Premier League double over West Ham for just the second time; however, the Hammers are unbeaten in their last eight home games against today's visitors, since a 2-1 loss in April 2011.
After Bowen is caught offside when through on goal, Aston Villa struggle to work their way past West Ham's closing down, as the home side try to apply early pressure.

Rogers and Watkins combine just outside the box, but West Ham captain Zouma stands firm to see off the threat of Duran, who proved his potency again on Thursday, when scoring a powerful strike against Ajax.
Martinez makes a rare error, carelessly gifting the ball to Soucek on the edge of Villa's area, but Tielemans rescues his goalkeeper just in time with a well-judged challenge.
For the first time, West Ham are having to sit back a little more, as Villa dictate play with some precise passing.
They've yet to make much progress into the final third, though.
A corner whipped in from the right by Bowen finds Paqueta on the edge of Villa's six-yard box, but the Brazilian's glancing header is steered comfortably over the crossbar.
SAVE! Bailey beats Emerson easily, then cuts a smart ball inside for Watkins, who appears on the right side of the area.
The Villa striker shoots low and hard from a very tight angle, but Areola is equal to it, making a sharp stop with his feet!
It's a confident start from Aston Villa, who are bossing the ball now, as West Ham struggle to lay a glove on their opponents.
The home side have become more and more passive, having only 29 per cent of possession.
Every claret-and-blue-clad West Ham player is back inside their own half, as they maintain a cautious defensive shape, hoping to draw Villa on and strike at speed on the counter.
Will that prove effective today?
CLOSE! Chances for both sides! As West Ham defenders back off, space opens up for Rogers, who tests Areola with a shot that the goalkeeper saves well.
Then, seconds later, Paqueta drives in a low effort at the other end, and a heavy deflection off Soucek sends it spinning just wide of the left-hand post!
As is customary for the Birmingham club under Unai Emery, Aston Villa are building gradually from the back, with goalkeeper Martinez heavily involved in the play.
West Ham are pressing a little higher now.
NO PENALTY! Emerson is sent back-tracking by Bailey again, and the latter's clipped ball into the box seems to strike his opponent's arm.
The referee signals that no penalty will be awarded, though, and the VAR also declines to intervene.
Earning his team a valuable free-kick, near the corner flag, Paqueta goes down under an eager challenge from Rogers.
That relieves some pressure for the home side.

SUPER STOP! After a superb ball is cut back by Bowen from the left byline, it trickles across the area, where Coufal finally arrives and unleashes a thunderbolt! The full-back's powerful drive is repelled by Martinez, who leaps across to make a fine save! West Ham are now imposing themselves on this game.
The home fans are buoyed, as their team push forward in numbers for the first time.
Villa are on the back foot now.

WEST HAM LEAD! Meeting a brilliant whipped cross from the right by Coufal, Antonio bravely dives to head home the Irons' opener: 1-0! He finds the bottom-left corner, leaving Martinez with no chance, and the hosts' growing pressure pays off!
From the right touchline, Coufal sends over an inviting delivery, which is met by the head of goalscorer Antonio.
Having done well to open the scoring, Antonio is now clutching his shoulder and looks in some pain.
His grimace suggests that he'll struggle to continue for much longer, but perhaps the injury can be assessed further at half-time.
Villa can't re-find their rhythm, as West Ham sense the chance to increase their lead before half-time.
This game has turned on its head over the past 10 minutes - under greater pressure, the away side have started to show cracks.
Paqueta is down on the turf, nursing what seems to be a knock to the calf.
Like Antonio before him, the Brazilian playmaker is thankfully able to recover quickly enough and returns to the fray.
West Ham have now scored 11 goals across their last three-and-a-half matches at the London Stadium, where their only defeat in 14 games was a humbling 6-0 defeat to Arsenal.
After a rocky spell, they're now showing signs that they can keep inching up the Premier League table.
Racing away down the left, after Lenglet loses the ball carelessly, Kudus reaches the area and tries his luck from a tight angle.
However, his firmly struck shot zips several feet wide of the near post - it was asking a lot to score from there.
After another inswinging corner by Bowen, initially headed away by Watkins, Kudus turns the ball into the net.

events.action: turns the ball into the net

text: However, the whistle has already been blown for a foul on Martinez.
Villa escape again.
Rather desperately, Douglas Luiz lines one up from over 20 yards out, only to crash his shot straight into Soucek.
Villa are proving short of ideas inside West Ham's half, and they seem to be missing McGinn's drive.
Three minutes of stoppage time are indicated by the fourth official, as Antonio bundles over Lenglet near the left byline.
That's a free-kick to Aston Villa.
Bailey drives past Kudus and Emerson and reaches the edge of West Ham's area, but the fleet-footed winger's pass inside is then cut out.
The hosts are defending their lead quite comfortably at the moment.
With a rare chance to shoot, Watkins flashes his shot across goal, sending the ball trundling well wide of the right-hand post.
Areola was not too concerned.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 1-0 ASTON VILLA

After a sluggish start, West Ham finally started to shake off their slumbers approaching the midpoint of a close-fought first half, and Antonio's headed goal sees them lead Aston Villa 1-0 at the break.

Villa began more brightly of two teams that were in European action just three days ago, but their lack of focus in midfield - and several misplaced passes at the back - invited the Irons to move out of a low defensive block and apply more attacking pressure.
Therefore, the hosts' goal was no surprise when it came, and their fourth-placed visitors have failed to provide much of a response since falling behind.

Villa are accustomed to leading at half-time - only Manchester City have done so more often in the Premier League this season - but they've only won once when trailing at the interval, ultimately losing on five other occasions.
Under Moyes, West Ham are capable of sitting deep and frustrating opponents, so they'll surely be confident of taking maximum points now, and closing the gap to sixth-placed Manchester United.
Unai Emery has reacted to his team's subdued showing by making a double change at half-time.
First, the ineffective Duran is replaced by France international Diaby.
Cash is also introduced, as Lenglet makes way.
Konsa should move inside to centre-back.
West Ham kick off, and we are back under way at the London Stadium!
Coufal's latest cross from the right flank strikes Rogers and spins behind for a corner-kick.
Villa's young winger is left winded momentarily, but the game will resume with another Bowen corner.
GOAL CHECK! West Ham score again.

Not for the first time, Bowen's set-piece delivery causes havoc in Villa's box, and his inswinging corner-kick is bundled past Martinez by Antonio from close range! However, the VAR has cut the hosts' joy short, as it seems that it may have been Antonio's arm that guided the ball home!
NO GOAL! West Ham's hopes of going 2-0 up are dashed! Antonio's finish was with his arm, so it's chalked off! Villa breathe again!
Trying to make the most of their let-off, Aston Villa are pressing forward now, seeking an equaliser.
Such an incident could even lift them out of mediocrity, as the Villans have lacked any spark today.
Tielemans brings down Kudus in midfield, killing the away side's building momentum.
West Ham take the chance to edge a few yards further up the pitch.
This time, Konsa is on hand to head away Bowen's latest inswinging corner, rising highest at the near post to clear the immediate danger.
West Ham have been causing plenty of problems with set-pieces, so it looks like Villa have altered their defensive strategy.
Aston Villa are yet to lose back-to-back Premier League matches this season, but they are just over half an hour away from suffering such a fate.
Meanwhile, West Ham are on course to extend their unbeaten run at home to the Villans to 10 top-flight games.
Antonio just fails to beat Konsa to the ball out on the left touchline, when he would have been in behind Villa's high defensive line.
West Ham always pose a threat on the break, so this final half-hour is fascinatingly poised.
Emerson makes a good block to divert Bailey's shot behind for a corner.
The Jamaican's subsequent set-piece is elaborately worked, but a move involving several team-mates ultimately comes to nothing - that was a waste.
With Villa still short of inspiration, Unai Emery opts for another double change: first, Moreno makes way for Digne at left-back.
The more direct Zaniolo is also introduced, as Rogers departs.
When the ball falls to Bailey on the right side of the box, he takes one touch to set himself but then leans back and skews his shot well over the crossbar.
Villa have managed only two shots on target so far.
Moyes now makes a move that seems designed to protect his team's slender lead: Antonio is replaced by Johnson.
Areola palms away Digne's dangerous cross from the left, as Villa continue to build pressure.
The visitors are offering more of a threat on the left flank since the French full-back's arrival.
SAVE! Aston Villa take another short corner, which is eventually worked out to Tielemans, around 25 yards from goal.
The Belgian's trademark long-range strike is punched away by Areola! It was just too centrally placed to cause the goalkeeper major problems.
Kudus cleverly drifts past Tielemans and then draws a foul from his opponent, who is then booked by the referee.

SAVE! From a 20-yard free-kick, Paqueta beats Villa's defensive wall with a curling shot - but not Martinez! The Brazilian's effort is not quite towards the bottom corner, so his South American counterpart is able to keep it out fairly comfortably.
At the end of another period of Villa pressure, Alvarez beats Cash in an aerial duel but concedes another corner.
West Ham are struggling to get out of their own half at the moment.

SHARP STOP! Areola is called upon again, as he first cuts out a dangerous low cross from the right, then keeps out Konsa's shot! The Villa defender drives a powerful effort on target from close range, but it's straight at the goalkeeper, who stands firm!
After Cash sprints into the box and clips over an inviting cross from the right, Johnson does well to scramble the ball away from danger, as West Ham hang on.
How long can they hold out?
VILLA PULL LEVEL! Two substitutes combine! Diaby dances away from Alvarez on the right, then pulls back a low pass for Zaniolo, who times his surge perfectly.
The Italy international thumps in an unstoppable finish from 10 yards out - and this time Areola can't save West Ham! It's 1-1: what a climax we have in prospect at the London Stadium!
Driving to the right byline at top speed, Diaby beats his man and then picks out Zaniolo's late burst into the box - that's his sixth Premier League assist of the season.
Kudus just runs out of steam, when it seems that he can stretch Villa's exposed defence on the counter.
Still, it's some positive intent from West Ham, following a passive spell that has cost them the lead.
Picking up his 10th booking of the Premier League season, Alvarez is penalised for becoming entangled with Zaniolo.
He'll have to serve a two-match ban.
Goalscorer Zaniolo is also shown a yellow card for his part in the confrontation with Alvarez.
Paqueta is now taken off, as Ward-Prowse jogs on.
Moyes also makes a straight swap at left-back, as Cresswell comes on for Emerson.
Another flashpoint arises, as the game becomes more testy in its final stages.
Kudus tussles with Douglas Luiz, and is perhaps lucky just to be shown a yellow card.
Douglas Luiz aggressively responds to being elbowed by Kudus and is also booked by the referee.
The yellow cards are coming thick and fast now, as Mavropanos goes into the book for delaying the restart.
West Ham are apparently hoping to see this game out for a point.
Aston Villa remain camped inside their hosts' half, and they seem likeliest to snatch a late winner.
Unai Emery's substitutions have helped turn the tide, but can the Champions League chasers complete their comeback?
There are to be at least seven additional minutes for stoppages - largely due to a flurry of bookings over the past few minutes - and that leaves time for either side to turn one point into three.

BRILLIANT BLOCK! A superb run up the right by Kudus opens up space, allowing Ward-Prowse to strike with power from near the penalty spot - but Cash dives in to make a goal-saving intervention! Surely that would have nestled in the net! Great defending!
Slowly but surely, West Ham are edging their way back into this game, as the clock ticks down.
They've managed to move a few more yards upfield, pushing Villa back for the first time in a while.

HAVE WEST HAM WON IT? With typical accuracy, Ward-Prowse delivers a dangerous free-kick into the box, before a desperate scramble ends with Soucek bundling the ball over the goal-line! He got the final touch, after Mavropanos tried to turn it home from a couple of yards out! That would be 2-1 to the Hammers, but will it stand? The VAR has got a lot to assess here, amid a chaotic scene! What a climax!
PITCHSIDE REVIEW! After a long review by the VAR, now the referee sprints over to the pitchside monitor for a look at Soucek's finish himself.
It seems he may have handled the ball in the process of prodding it in via Bowen's body!

GOAL RULED OUT! West Ham's winner is chalked off! There was a handball offence as Soucek turned in an attempted shot by Mavropanos, so it remains 1-1 at the London Stadium! The home fans are in uproar!
After such a dramatic moment, the energy seems to have been sucked out of this game, as both sides are on course to share the spoils.
West Ham were so close to winning it late on, but the final whistle will come any moment now.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 1-1 ASTON VILLA
West Ham have to settle for a point at home to Aston Villa, as the home side are twice denied by the VAR during an eventful second half that ends 1-1 at London Stadium.
Between both efforts being chalked off, Villa scored an equaliser through substitute Zaniolo, following Antonio's first-half header.

Either side enjoyed periods of dominance, in a rather uneven encounter that came shortly after European triumphs for the two clubs - Villa bossed the ball, but their hosts were sharper from set-pieces.
As a result of this draw, the visitors increase their advantage over Tottenham to three points in the Premier League table, while West Ham are now within three of Manchester United.
The Irons visit Newcastle United after the international break; Villa will host Wolves.
That's all from today's live coverage, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
